label: Higher at D1 after reward or reaching S1; higher at GO/D2 when S2 favoured or after a2.
explanation: Raw reset gate r33 (D2 high, GO low). At D1 it adds up roughly linearly from the last trial: rewarded is about +0.2, reached S1 is about +0.1 to +0.2, chose a2 is about +0.2 (a1 S2 u is lowest at -0.36, a2 S1 r highest at +0.2). Over all phases, and most at GO and D2, it goes down as the observer belief that S1 is good goes up (belief_lo weight is negative), and it is higher after an a2 choice. The free fit adds: at D2, a low value after a rare a1->S2 transition (observed at D2); at GO, a lower value after a reward; a separate D1 a2 term; and a D1 S2-unrewarded dip. These take dev R^2 from about 0.55 to 0.72. The largest remaining misses are window-first trials, where the previous trial is unknown. The future reward contributes almost nothing (reference score 0.01). Only observed variables are used.

issues: The label leaves out the a2 effect at D1. The profile residuals show D1 after a2 S2 u at -0.18 against a1 S2 u at -0.36, and a2 S1 u at +0.06 against a1 S1 u at -0.135, so choosing a2 raises D1 by about 0.18. The short form has no D1 action term. Misses on the recorded short form confirm this with large systematic over-predictions at D1 after a1: a1 S2 u -0.216, a1 S1 u -0.165, a1 S2 r -0.149.

At GO, reward lowers the gate, the opposite of its effect at D1. The residuals are GO after a1 S1 r -0.19 and after a2 S1 r -0.04, against a2 S1 u +0.22. The short form misses this: GO after a2 S1 u and a2 S2 u are under-predicted by +0.098 and +0.087. Neither the label nor the short form says the reward effect flips sign.

The claim 'higher at GO/D2 after a2' mostly holds at GO. At D2 the previous-trial a2 effect is weak once belief is accounted for. Splitting the term to (phase==GO)*(prev_action==2) gives test 0.517, against 0.537 for (phase!=D1).

The score depends heavily on how the first trial of a window (previous trial unknown, prev_action and prev_state = -1) is coded. Adding +(prev_action==2) inside the D1 sum drops test R^2 to 0.474. Adding -(prev_action==1), which differs only in how unknown trials are coded, raises it to 0.593. So the recorded 0.537 is fragile, and part of the D1 term works as a fitted correction for first trials.

Unmodelled in the recorded form: the current-trial a1->S2 (rare) dip at D2, residual -0.235. Misses show D2 after a1 S2 r under-predicted by +0.109 and the worst windows have D2 S2R cells predicted about 0.2-0.3 too high. This variable is observed at D2.

A better short form exists that passes --short: '(phase==D1)*(prev_reward - (prev_state==2) - (prev_action==1)) ;; belief_lo ;; (phase==GO)*((prev_action==2) - prev_reward)' scores test R^2 beyond timing 0.624, against 0.537. Its misses are smaller and more balanced (mean error per phase within 0.013). The largest remaining cells are D1 after a1 S1 r +0.146 and D1 after an unknown previous trial -0.094. An alternative ending in (phase==D2)*(action==1)*(state==2) scores 0.605.
skeptic.revised_label: D1: raised by last reward, reaching S1, choosing a2; GO: a2 raises, reward lowers; falls with S1 belief.
